title: Major changes in Team India: Doeschate steps down; Subhadeep replaces Dilip
content:
Ryan ten Doeschate has stepped down as India's men's assistant coach, bringing an end to his two-year stint with the national team, while Subhadeep Ghosh will be India's new fielding coach after T Dilip's contract came to an end and was not renewed, TOI has learnt.
Ten Doeschate and Dilip's final assignment was India's white-ball tour of England. Both will, thus, not travel with Team India for their two-Test tour of Sri Lanka in August, while it will be the first international assignment for Subhadeep, who has been the fielding coach of India A teams in the past.
During India's England tour, Ten Doeschate informed the
BCCI of his decision to leave, despite being offered an extension until 2027 by the board. Although the BCCI was keen to retain him, the former Netherlands all-rounder declined the offer, citing personal reasons. With a young family, Ten Doeschate opted to step away from the demands of international cricket and its relentless travel schedule.
Meanwhile, fielding coach T Dilip is parting ways with the national team following the completion of his tenure. He will not travel with the squad for the upcoming Test tour of Sri Lanka.
Ten Doeschate joined the Indian coaching setup in July 2024 after former India opener Gautam Gambhir succeeded Rahul Dravid as the head coach following India's T20 World Cup triumph. Having worked closely with Gambhir during their successful stint at Kolkata Knight Riders, the former Netherlands all-rounder was brought into the national setup by Gambhir alongside bowling coach Morne Morkel.
During Ten Doeschate's stint, India won the Champions Trophy and the Asia Cup in 2025 and successfully defended the 2026 T20 World Cup, although the Test side endured a difficult period, losing the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia before suffering series defeats against New Zealand (3-0) and South Africa (2-0) at home.

title: FIDE reveals host city for Gukesh vs Sindarov World Championship clash
content:
The International Chess Federation (FIDE) has announced Geneva, Switzerland, as the host city for the 2026 FIDE World Championship Match, where reigning champion Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his crown against Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov in what promises to be a historic showdown.
The World Championship match will be held from November 25 to December 15, with both Gukesh and Sindarov set to be 20 years old when the contest begins, making it the youngest World Championship match in chess history.
Geneva chosen as neutral venue for historic showdown
Announcing the venue, FIDE interim president
Viswanathan Anand said several countries had shown strong interest in staging the prestigious event before the governing body opted for a neutral venue.
"Several countries expressed a strong interest in hosting the FIDE World Championship Match, including India, the United States and Cyprus. After carefully considering all the proposals, FIDE has decided to stage the match on neutral soil and bring it to Geneva, a city with a historic tradition of bringing nations and cultures together," Anand said.
"We look forward to welcoming the global chess community to Switzerland. The local chess fans will have the opportunity to experience world-class chess in person, while millions of fans around the globe can follow the battle online as the duel for the highest title in chess unfolds."
The announcement means Switzerland will once again host a World Championship match, more than two decades after Brissago staged the title clash in 2004.
Swiss Chess Federation President André Vögtlin hailed the decision as a landmark moment for chess in the country.
"This is a truly special day for Swiss chess. Twenty-two years after Brissago, an event of global chess significance is returning to Switzerland. For us, this is far more than wonderful news – it's a defining moment for chess in our country, one that fills us with both joy and motivation," Vögtlin said.
He added that hosting the event would provide a significant boost to the game's popularity across Switzerland.
"It's also a unique opportunity to raise the public profile of chess in Switzerland even further and to inspire new players to take up our sport. Over the coming weeks, we'll be sharing regular updates on how we're using this mega-event to boost the popularity of the 'royal game' in our country," he added.
Youngest World Championship match in history
The Geneva contest will pit two of chess's brightest young stars against each other for the sport's biggest prize.
Gukesh will defend the title he won in Singapore in December 2024, when he defeated Ding Liren in the 14th and final classical game to become the youngest undisputed World Champion at the age of 18.
Sindarov, meanwhile, secured his place in the title match by winning the 2026 FIDE Candidates Tournament in Cyprus with a round to spare, adding another major achievement to his triumph at the 2025 FIDE World Cup.
The championship match will consist of 14 classical games, with the first player to reach 7.5 points being declared the winner. If the scores are level after all 14 games, the title will be decided through tiebreaks.
FIDE said further details regarding the tournament schedule, ticket sales, spectator access, media accreditation and accompanying events will be announced in the coming weeks as anticipation builds for one of the most eagerly awaited World Championship clashes in recent history.
